question: Explain why the average intensity due to two incoherent waves is simply the sum of their individual intensities.

options.A: In incoherent addition, the fixed phase difference makes $\cos\phi=1$, so $I=(\sqrt{I_1}+\sqrt{I_2})^2$.
options.B: Incoherent waves always cancel, so average intensity is zero.
options.C: For two waves, $I=I_1+I_2+2\sqrt{I_1I_2}\cos\phi$. For incoherent waves, $\phi$ varies randomly, so the time average of $\cos\phi$ is zero. Therefore, average intensity is $I_1+I_2$.
options.D: The average intensity of incoherent waves is $I_1-I_2$.
